messages:
cust_acme_ops: Hey, heads up — after our app pinned to the locked model this morning (model: text-embed-arc-2048:locked) our embedding pipeline started failing. Previously vectors were 1536, now responses are 1024 and our index rejects the docs. Errors look like: 

cust_acme_ops: error from ingestion: 'vector length mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024' (bulk insert id=ingest-2026-03-17-08)

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you share a sample request/response (with any keys scrubbed) and the exact model id you pinned to? Also, did you use any quantized variant? :eyes:

cust_acme_ops: We pinned via the console to the 'locked' tag, the model catalog showed text-embed-arc-2048:locked. Here's a redacted API call: 

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "text-embed-arc-2048:locked",
  "input": ["doc1 text", "doc2 text"]
}
```

And response (first vector trimmed): 

```
{
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.0012, -0.0034, ...(1024 floats total)]},
    {"embedding": [0.0009, -0.0021, ...]}
  ]
}
```

alice_support: Thanks — that makes it clear. I'm escalating to Eng-ML to triage why the locked tag changed vector width. Filing as high priority. :triage_flag:

ben_ml: I dug into the model catalog + rollout logs. Summary: during the canary roll earlier, the canary used the new embed head (1024) for the model family 'arc-embed', but the pinned/locked metadata was not updated — the catalog mapping for the locked tag pointed to the canary binary by mistake. So requests with :locked were routed to the canary flavor that emits 1024-d vectors. Looks like a metadata/staging mismatch, not a runtime quantization truncation.

ben_ml: Evidence: catalog entry for text-embed-arc-2048:locked shows git-sha `g7f2c` but binaries on nodes were `g7f2c-canary` with embed_head=1024. Canary->locked flip happened during the automated promotion job at 07:42 UTC.

alice_support: That explains the sudden change. What are immediate mitigations for the customer? They have a large index (millions) and can't re-ingest easily.

ben_ml: Short-term options: 
- Route their tenant to the previous model variant (text-embed-arc-1536:v2025-11-09) via a tenant-level override. This preserves 1536 vectors.
- If they must stay on :locked, we can deploy a compatibility shim that pads/truncates to 1536 automatically (not ideal, quality loss).
- Re-ingest with new dims (longer-term).

carla_oncall: I'll push a hotfix to routing to respect the explicit `variant` field when present and roll back the catalog pointer for :locked to the correct sha. Deploying change to control plane now. deploy-bot, kick a canary? :wrench:

deploy-bot: Deploy request accepted. Starting canary deploy: control-plane-routing-fix-2026-03-17 (canary id cp-8891). Rolling to 4 control-plane instances.

carla_oncall: Hotfix pushed to canary, monitoring. Also added a temporary runtime assert that will return a warning header `X-Embed-Vecsize` with the declared vec size, so clients can detect mismatches before bulk ingestion.

alice_support: Customer, do you want us to apply the tenant override now to point to the older variant? We can do that while patch finishes rolling out. :thumbsup:

cust_acme_ops: Please do the override now. We prefer rollback to older variant to avoid reindexing today. Appreciate the quick escalation. :pray:

alice_support: Done — I applied tenant override to `text-embed-arc-1536:v2025-11-09` at 08:05 UTC for tenant acme-corp. Can you confirm you see 1536-length vectors again?

cust_acme_ops: Confirmed — embeddings are back at 1536. Ingestion resumed successfully. Thanks for the fast help.

ben_ml: Follow-ups we're doing: 
- Add vec_size metadata to model catalog entries (already in progress).
- Add a model preflight endpoint `/v1/models/{id}/metadata` returning `vec_size` so clients can programmatically validate before ingest.
- Add an automated check in the promotion pipeline to prevent promoting canary-only config to a locked tag without explicit approval.

carla_oncall: Also adding an alert to the ops dashboard when a locked tag's resolved sha differs from the intended locked-sha in the release plan. Should reduce this class of human/catalog drift.

alice_support: I'll update the customer with remediation steps and timeline for the catalog fixes. Closing the immediate incident; moving follow-up tasks to ENG-ML backlog under ticket ML-embed-342. :white_check_mark:

cust_acme_ops: Thanks everyone — appreciate the clear remediation and roadmap.

alice_support: Marking thread resolved. If anything else pops up ping #support or reopen this thread. :wave:
